subject: openlumara
title: tools_load meta-tool keeps the tool array near-empty; AI-loaded tool sets persist per chat and self-heal via rejection messages
one_why: Baseline tool surface is one meta-tool listing enabled modules; a call to an unloaded tool returns an actionable 'load it first with module_name=X' rejection instead of a failure, and the chat's loaded-module set is persisted/restored on resume - direct convergence with the seeded lazy-loading lineage (GPL: concepts-only).

subject: openlumara
title: Compaction writes a SUMMARIZATION_CUTOFF marker instead of deleting history - model view is cut, user history survives, deletion of the marker reverts
one_why: LLM summary + cutoff signal are appended as ordinary messages; context.get() slices everything before the last cutoff and prepends 'Summarize our chat so far.', so compression is revertible from the UI with no separate checkpoint store.

subject: openlumara
title: At 80% of context the model itself receives a budget warning and is instructed to tell the user to /compress
one_why: Cost visibility is routed through the agent rather than only the UI: provider usage receipts cached on the chat drive an end-prompt injection, making the AI a stakeholder in its own context budget.

subject: openlumara
title: HTTP module resolves DNS, validates every resolved address (incl. IPv4-mapped IPv6 unwrapping) against a full blocklist, and re-validates on redirects
one_why: Unparseable literals treated as unsafe, CGNAT/link-local/metadata ranges covered, plus dangerous-port blocklist, https-only default, and per-minute rate cap - the complete SSRF package for a personal agent (GPL: concepts-only).

subject: openlumara
title: Six-layer regex/Unicode injection screening of web content plus random-delimiter untrusted-data envelopes
one_why: Zero-width + homoglyph + base64-decode-and-scan + instruction-density layers, then content fenced with a 32-char crypto-random delimiter and doubled security notices; honest nuance: regex layers are bypassable, the envelope fence is the part worth keeping.

subject: openlumara
title: api_bridge defaults api_key_required=False and executes every request with commands_authorized=True
one_why: Enabling the OpenAI-compatible endpoint gives any network caller privileged slash-command execution (framework commands bypass the AI entirely) unless the operator notices one boolean; no SECURITY.md to flag it.

subject: openlumara
title: Shell sandbox ships with internet on: setting default True vs in-code fallback False
one_why: The jail is otherwise solid (cap-drop ALL, read-only rootfs, no-new-privileges, pids/mem/cpu caps, gVisor auto-detect) but the persisted default is internet_access=True, and a config-drift read would silently flip to the opposite fallback - network-egress-off should be the default.

subject: openlumara
title: WebUI session middleware falls back to the literal 'openlumara-default-session-secret-change-me'
one_why: Login is rate-limited and constant-time-compared, but session cookies are signed with a publicly-known key unless the user sets session_secret, so forged sessions defeat the login gate on exposed instances.

subject: openlumara
title: Recursive agentic tool loop has no iteration cap, loop detection, or budget
one_why: process() recurses per tool-call round with only a per-tool 10s timeout; a model ping-ponging between tools burns context and spend unbounded - crush is the only anchor with a breaker, and this loop lacks one entirely.

subject: openlumara
title: 1597 commits, 29k LOC, zero automated tests and no CI; the one test-named file is an interactive TTY viewer
evidence: channels/turn_grouping_test.py:1-31; no .github/ or any CI config in tree
one_why: QA is manual-review culture (commit messages say so); nothing in the repo can prove loop, context-trim, or sandbox-flag behavior, which caps verification at 1 regardless of how the code reads.

subject: openlumara
title: Scheduler jobs pick a per-job prompt strategy trading token cost against provider prompt-cache reuse
one_why: Three explicit modes (instruction-only / system+instruction / full-context) with the full-context mode chosen for cache-hit economics - a rare explicit statement of the cache-vs-tokens tradeoff at the scheduling layer (GPL: concepts-only).
